title: Midnight heuristics riff — Morgan Reyes
content:
Quick late-night brain dump on candidate (initial loop) — notes to self and proposed next steps.

Context:
- Role: Senior Runtime Engineer (low-latency serving/runtime)
- Interview loop: system design + take-home discussion + 45m coding
- Candidate: referred by internal eng (no public repo for core work)

High-level read: capable engineer, strong infra instincts, voice-of-production. Hypothesis: could be a strong IC3/IC4 depending on follow-ups.

Signals — positives:
- Clear on tradeoffs between batching and latency; had concrete examples from past infra where they tuned batching windows to meet a p99 SLA (described metrics/measurement loops).
- Good mental model for KV caching and cache invalidation patterns; sketched an approach that avoided global locks and used lease-based invalidation (practical).
- Comfortable with quantization/FP work — understands end-to-end quality tradeoffs (loss vs perf) and how to instrument regressions.
- Communication: concise, asks clarifying Qs early, surfaces operational concerns (observability, rollout safety) rather than just code correctness.

Risks / red flags:
- Coding phase had a couple of small bugs around edge-case I/O handling; fixed quickly but relied on unit-testing assumptions. Not a huge deal but worth probing for test culture.
- Slightly light on distributed-systems proofs: comfortable with patterns but less confident deriving latencies under churn (we should probe more on failure modes + backpressure).
- No obvious leadership examples in prior role (led features but not full cross-team rollouts). For IC4+ we'd want a clear example.

Open questions to close in follow-up:
- Ownership examples: ask for a 2–3 week rollout they owned end-to-end (incidents, stakeholders, KPIs).
- Failure mode thought-experiment: simulate network partition + autoscaler flapping — what are the first 3 alarms, and what mitigation order do they choose?
- Testing/CI culture: how do they approach flaky tests and infra-level deterministic checks?

Suggested tactical next steps:
- Short 30m follow-up with SRE (Benji) to run the failure-mode scenario and focus on observability + instrumentation ideas.
- Request a short write-up (1 page) describing a past rollout they led or a hypothetical rollout plan for migrating a model version with 0% latency regression — use bullet form. Deadline: 72 hours.
- If comfortable, run a small pairing session on a unit test that reproduces the coding-phase bug (to see the remediation approach).

Provisional scorecard (my internal yardstick, 1-5):
- System design: 4
- Coding/implementation: 3.5
- Reliability & SRE mindset: 4
- Cross-team leadership: 3
- Overall hire propensity: Strong maybe (bring back for SRE probe)

Notes to self (rubber-sheet items — rough, actionable):
- Emphasize productization: ask how they balance quick fixes vs technical debt in prod. I got the sense they prefer practical pragmatism but want an explicit example.
- Watch for "pattern recitation" vs deep-first principles — they sometimes reach for patterns without deriving metrics; probe with numbers.
- If we get a write-up, evaluate: clarity, measurable KPIs, rollback plan, stakeholder comms. That will be the tiebreaker for IC4.

Slack nudge template (short):
"Hey Benji — can you do a 30m failure-mode probe with Morgan this week? Focus on observability + escalation plan. I left specific probe notes in their file. Thanks!"

TODOs (my inbox):
- [ ] Schedule Benji probe (target Thu)
- [ ] Send write-up request + set 72h deadline
- [ ] Prepare pairing repo fragment to reproduce coding bug (small harness)

End of dump. Sleep now.

-- Morgan
